summary: SEEK salary text carries superannuation percentages that are not pay; a name query can match several advertisers; a saved search may be defined only by secondary filters; and hiring-volume deltas must compare adjacent calendar periods, not adjacent populated buckets.
reason: Review of the initial hand-authored novel commands surfaced four domain-shape bugs: ParseSalary read '11%' in '$55/hr + 11% super' as a rate; `company` blended distinct advertisers under one substring match; `me new-jobs` skipped filter-only saved searches; `trends` omitted empty months/weeks before differencing. Each is a property of the SEEK data, so a regen must re-apply the same guards.
validated_outcome: go test ./... passes; ParseSalary('$90k + 11% super') -> ~$90k (was rejected); bucketRange materialises every period across the window.
